Title: Synaptics’ shares rise after two acquisitions, strong earnings
Summary: Synaptics Inc. saw its shares rise after announcing the acquisition of Conexant Systems LLC and Marvell Technology Group's Multimedia Solutions Business for a combined value of approximately $395 million plus Synaptics stock. These acquisitions are expected to expand Synaptics' market opportunity by $2.8 billion and strategically position it in the consumer Internet of Things market. The company also reported strong third-quarter earnings, exceeding Wall Street projections.

Title: Marvell Technology Group in Advanced Talks to Combine With Cavium
Summary: Marvell Technology Group is in advanced talks to merge with Cavium Inc., potentially creating a chip maker valued at approximately $14 billion. Cavium shareholders are expected to receive a modest premium in the deal, which could be announced within weeks if discussions progress favorably. Marvell previously had a market value of about $9 billion, while Cavium's was over $4 billion.

Title: Santa Clara's Marvell may buy San Jose's Cavium to form $14B chipmaker
Summary: Marvell Technology Group is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire Cavium, potentially forming a $14 billion chip company. The deal, if completed, would combine two significant players in the semiconductor industry based in Silicon Valley. Discussions are expected to conclude in the coming weeks.

Title: Marvell Semiconductor President and CEO Matt Murphy Elected Chair of SIA
Summary: The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) announced the election of Matt Murphy, President and CEO of Marvell Semiconductor, Inc., as its 2018 Chair, and Sanjay Mehrotra, President and CEO of Micron Technology, Inc., as its 2018 Vice Chair. Murphy highlighted the importance of U.S. support for research, competitiveness, and global trade for continued progress in the semiconductor industry. Mehrotra emphasized unifying efforts through SIA to maintain U.S. leadership in semiconductor manufacturing, design, and research.

Title: Marvell Technology clinches roughly $6 billion deal to buy Cavium: Sources
Summary: Marvell Technology has agreed to acquire Cavium for around $6 billion to expand its presence in the networking equipment sector and diversify its business beyond traditional storage devices. The cash-and-stock deal is expected to be announced on Monday and stems from Marvell CEO Matt Murphy's restructuring efforts. Cavium, with a market capitalization of $5.2 billion, produces network, security, server, and switching processors and systems.

Title: Marvell Technology to buy rival chipmaker Cavium for $6 billion
Summary: Marvell Technology Group Ltd announced its acquisition of rival chipmaker Cavium Inc for approximately $6 billion. This strategic move aims to expand Marvell's wireless connectivity business and strengthen its competitive position in the rapidly consolidating semiconductor industry. The deal, led by CEO Matthew Murphy, reflects efforts to counteract declining demand for Marvell's traditional chip products and better compete with industry giants like Intel and Qualcomm.

Title: Bermuda’s Marvell agrees $6bn takeover deal
Summary: Marvell Technology Group Ltd, a Bermuda-domiciled microchip maker, has agreed to acquire Cavium for $6 billion. The deal involves Marvell paying $40 in cash plus 2.1757 Marvell common shares for each Cavium share, financed in part by $1.75 billion in debt. This acquisition is seen as a strategic move to enable both companies to better compete with semiconductor industry giants, including Intel, Qualcomm Inc, and Broadcom Ltd, and is expected to add 10 percent to the combined company's annual profit through cost savings.

Title: Exclusive: Marvell cuts jobs following Cavium acquisition
Summary: Marvell is cutting 44 jobs at its Santa Clara headquarters as part of a new round of layoffs. These cutbacks are occurring as the semiconductor manufacturing company integrates its recent acquisition of San Jose-based Cavium. Marvell is implementing both local and statewide reductions in its workforce.

Title: Marvell cuts more positions following Cavium merger
Summary: Semiconductor company Marvell Technology Group Ltd. is implementing additional job cuts after its $6 billion merger with Cavium Inc. this summer. This follows earlier job reductions announced in the wake of the acquisition. The company had previously approved the $6 billion purchase to form a larger chipmaker.

Title: NXP to Buy Marvell Wi-Fi Tech Unit in $1.76 Billion Deal
Summary: NXP Semiconductors NV has agreed to acquire Marvell Technology Group Ltd.'s Wi-Fi connectivity business for $1.76 billion in an all-cash deal. This acquisition includes Marvell’s Wi-Fi and Bluetooth technology and assets. The move will enable NXP, the largest chip supplier to the automotive industry, to broaden its offerings for connecting devices to the internet.

Title: NXP to buy Marvell's WiFi, Bluetooth business for $1.76 billion
Summary: Dutch chipmaker NXP Semiconductors NV announced its acquisition of Marvell Technology Group Ltd's wireless connectivity business for $1.76 billion in cash. This strategic move aims to expand NXP's product portfolio for industrial, automotive, and communication infrastructure markets, with Marvell's unit expected to double its 2019 revenue of $300 million by 2022. The deal, anticipated to close by Q1 2020, will help NXP cross-sell products and aligns with Marvell's focus on the network equipment market.

Title: NXP Announces $1.76 Billion Purchase Of Marvell Wi-Fi Business
Summary: NXP Semiconductors NV is acquiring Marvell Technology Group's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth product lines for $1.76 billion in an all-cash deal expected to close by the end of 2020. This acquisition follows NXP's failed takeover by Qualcomm and is seen as a strategic move to bolster NXP's automotive product offerings and Wi-Fi technologies, despite some industry experts questioning the premium price paid especially with the rise of 5G. NXP believes Wi-Fi will remain dominant for the next five years, justifying the investment.

Title: Marvell Unveils Industry’s Lowest Power PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD Controllers
Summary: Marvell has introduced the industry's lowest power PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD controller portfolio, designed for next-generation data centers and edge devices. These new controllers offer unparalleled performance-power benefits, leveraging 12nm process technology and supporting various form factors. Industry leaders like AMD, Lenovo's Union Memory, Micron Technology, and Toshiba Memory Corporation have expressed support for Marvell's new technology, highlighting its potential to enable innovative, low-power, and high-performance SSD solutions.

Title: SEC fines Marvell Technology $5.5M in revenue manipulation scheme
Summary: The SEC fined Marvell Technology Group Ltd. $5.5 million for misleading investors by using an undisclosed revenue management procedure to meet publicly issued revenue guidance. The company orchestrated "pull-in" sales, accelerating future sales into the current quarter, which masked a decline in customer demand and loss of market share. Marvell settled the charges without admitting or denying the findings, agreeing to a cease and desist order and paying the penalty.

Title: Marvell Completes Acquisition of Aquantia
Summary: Marvell announced the completion of its acquisition of Aquantia, a pioneer in Multi-Gig Ethernet technology. This acquisition is expected to enhance Marvell's networking platform with Aquantia's innovative solutions and engineering talent, particularly strengthening its position in high-speed in-vehicle networking for autonomous driving. Aquantia's Chairman and CEO, Faraj Aalaei, will join Marvell in a senior leadership role.

Title: CFO Jean Hu helps turn Marvell Technology into a $18B company
Summary: Jean Hu, CFO of Marvell Technology Group, is credited with transforming the company from a "big startup" into an $18 billion enterprise. Board chairman Rick Hill praised her deep knowledge of numbers and straightforward approach to accounting. The article highlights her significant impact on the company's financial growth and stability.

Title: Marvell Semiconductor lays off close to 100 people at Santa Clara HQ
Summary: Marvell Semiconductor is cutting 124 jobs, with 94 of those positions located at its Santa Clara headquarters. This move contributes to over 1,200 tech industry layoffs in Silicon Valley since the beginning of the year, including at least 345 among chipmakers. The article also lists other recent layoffs at companies such as Intel, VMware, StubHub, and 8x8.

Title: Marvell Technology stock jumps on key partnerships with Nokia and Samsung
Summary: Marvell Technology Group's stock jumped over 9% following announcements of key 5G infrastructure partnerships with both Nokia Corp. and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. These collaborations, intended to enhance 5G network performance and efficiency, coincided with Marvell's strong fiscal fourth-quarter financial results which exceeded Wall Street's expectations. The company also provided positive guidance for the next quarter, factoring in potential coronavirus impacts.

Title: Large semiconductor company set to expand Boise presence
Summary: Marvell Semiconductor, a California-based firm, is set to expand its Boise, ID presence by leasing a 28,590 square foot building near Park Blvd. The expansion involves revamping the Clearwater Building into new office space capable of accommodating up to 444 employees, a project valued at $2.9 million. Marvell, which partners with Micron Technology, currently employs over 6,000 people globally and generates more than $2.9 billion in annual revenue.

Title: Marvell exits the general purpose Arm server business
Summary: Marvell Technology Group has announced it is discontinuing its ThunderX3 Arm-based server processor for general-purpose server use. The company will instead focus on vertical markets and hyperscalers, customizing silicon for major cloud providers. This move allows Marvell to secure up-front commitments and reduce risk by co-funding custom chip development with customers.

Title: Marvell Enabling the Next Generation of Data Center and Automotive AI Accelerator ASICs
Summary: Marvell announced its custom application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) offering is poised to enable next-generation AI accelerators for data centers and automotive markets. The company's ASICs feature advanced density SRAMs, high-performance SerDes, and pre-qualified high-bandwidth memory interfaces, ensuring rapid time-to-market. Marvell is collaborating with companies like Groq, which is developing the industry's first peta operations per second (POP/s) AI accelerator-on-a-chip using Marvell's ASIC technology.

Title: Marvell Announces $10 Billion Deal in Latest Chip Merger
Summary: Marvell Technology Group announced its acquisition of data center component chip maker Inphi for $10 billion. This merger aims to strengthen Marvell's position as a competitor in the infrastructure and data center markets. The deal was reported early Thursday.

Title: Marvell Acquires Inphi For Cloud Push
Summary: Marvell has announced its acquisition of Inphi for $10 billion, an all-cash-and-stock deal aimed at strengthening its position in cloud data centers and 5G technology. The acquisition is part of a broader consolidation trend in the chip sector, following other major deals like AMD's purchase of Xilinx and Nvidia's acquisition of ARM. Marvell plans to re-domicile in the United States, creating a "US semiconductor powerhouse" with an enterprise value of approximately $40 billion, leveraging Inphi's high-speed data interconnect platform for cloud infrastructure.

Title: Marvell to Acquire Inphi - Accelerating Growth and Leadership in Cloud and 5G Infrastructure
Summary: Marvell Technology Group Ltd. announced its definitive agreement to acquire Inphi Corporation in a cash and stock transaction, valued at approximately $40 billion, to enhance its leadership in cloud and 5G infrastructure. This acquisition will expand Marvell's addressable market, reinforce its customer base, and is expected to generate $125 million in annual run-rate synergies, becoming accretive to Marvell's non-GAAP earnings per share within the first year after closing. The combined company aims for end-to-end technology leadership in data infrastructure by merging Marvell's storage, networking, processor, and security portfolio with Inphi's electro-optics interconnect platform.

Title: Marvell Tech to acquire Inphi in stock-and-cash deal that is second in chip sector this week
Summary: Marvell Technology Group Ltd. announced its agreement to acquire Inphi Corp. in a cash and stock deal, creating a semiconductor company with an enterprise value of $40 billion. Marvell will pay $66 in cash and 2.323 shares for each Inphi share, with existing Marvell shareholders owning 83% of the combined company. This marks the second significant acquisition in the chip sector this week, following AMD's acquisition of Xilinx Inc.

Title: Marvell to buy Inphi in $10bn semiconductor deal
Summary: Semiconductor company Marvell Technology Group is set to acquire Inphi Corp in a $10 billion cash-and-stock deal. The acquisition aims to strengthen Marvell's leadership in cloud infrastructure and expand its 5G presence, leveraging Inphi's expertise in fiber-optic data traffic and its customer base including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Facebook. This move is part of a broader trend of consolidation within the semiconductor industry.

Title: Marvell Acquires Inphi in Cloud and 5G Push
Summary: Marvell Technology Group announced its acquisition of Inphi Corp. in a cash-and-stock deal estimated at up to $10 billion, aiming to accelerate growth in cloud and 5G infrastructure. This move will create a "U.S. semiconductor powerhouse" by combining Inphi's silicon photonics for optical interconnects with Marvell's copper interconnects, expanding Marvell's footprint in the networking industry. Analysts view the deal positively, noting it will increase Marvell's exposure to data center and 5G markets and diversify its offerings.

Title: Marvell Expands Borderless Enterprise Portfolio with Industry-Leading Octal Scalable mGig PHY Family
Summary: Marvell has introduced its second-generation Alaska Octal Scalable mGig PHY family, designed to enhance enterprise networking infrastructure with improved performance, cable reach, and lower power consumption. These new PHYs, including the Octal mGig-10G 88X3580 and Octal mGig-5G 88E2580, are part of Marvell's comprehensive borderless enterprise portfolio, offering scalable multi-Gigabit solutions optimized for emerging mobility and cloud applications. The devices provide power reductions of up to 10% and exceed IEEE cable reach requirements, making them suitable for high-bandwidth deployments like Wi-Fi 6 access points and HD security cameras.

Title: Marvell Introduces Carrier-Optimized Ethernet Access and Edge Switches
Summary: Marvell has introduced its new Prestera DX 7300 series of Ethernet switches, designed to optimize data movement in carrier access and metro networks. These switches support high-performance 5G deployments and 400GE metro optical transport services by integrating features like accurate time synchronization, MACsec, and advanced processing. The Prestera DX 7300 family aims to meet the stringent demands of modern network infrastructure with low power consumption and a small footprint.

Title: RISC-V And Marvell Technologies Advances Enable Storage Solutions
Summary: The article discusses how RISC-V computing and Marvell Technologies' advancements are driving innovation in storage solutions. It highlights presentations from the 2020 RISC-V Summit, detailing Western Digital's and Seagate's utilization of RISC-V processors for their storage devices, including customized SSDs and enhanced HDD control. Marvell's contributions, such as Data Processor Units (DPUs), NVMe over Fabric support, Ethernet Bunch of Flash, and solutions for next-gen HDDs, are also explored, emphasizing their role in advancing data center, automotive, and edge storage.

Title: Marvell Storage Solutions Power Toshiba's 18TB Cloud-Scale Capacity HDD
Summary: Marvell announced that its HDD controller and preamplifier are powering Toshiba's new MG09 Series 18TB Cloud-Scale HDDs, extending their long-standing collaboration. This technology enables Toshiba to meet the rapidly increasing demand for high-capacity storage in cloud data centers, driven by digital transformation and the proliferation of cloud services, AI, and 5G. The MG09 series utilizes innovative microwave-assisted magnetic recording (MAMR) technology and advanced signal processing, leveraging Marvell's expertise to deliver optimal rack space efficiency, reliability, and power efficiency.

Title: Marvell Technology’s Sales Got a Lift From 5G. Its Outlook Was Mixed,
Summary: Marvell Technology Group reported revenue exceeding Wall Street expectations, driven by 5G, and its adjusted profit met analyst models. However, the company's forecast for the current quarter suggested that future results might not be as robust as anticipated, raising concerns amidst the ongoing global chip shortage.

Title: Samsung and Marvell Unveil New System-on-a-Chip to Advance 5G Networks
Summary: Samsung and Marvell have jointly developed a new System-on-a-Chip (SoC) designed to significantly enhance 5G network performance, particularly for Massive MIMO and other advanced radios. This SoC, targeted for market introduction to Tier One operators in Q2 2021, promises to improve cellular radio capacity and coverage while reducing power consumption by up to 70% compared to previous solutions. The collaboration aims to provide operators with a competitive edge in 5G deployment through optimized performance and power efficiency.

Title: Marvell closes on $10 billion Inphi deal, expanding data center and 5G business
Summary: Marvell Technology has completed its $10 billion acquisition of Inphi after receiving approval from Chinese regulators, expanding its reach into data centers and 5G network infrastructure. CEO Matt Murphy noted the deal's overwhelmingly positive global customer support. The acquisition will enhance Marvell's growth in key markets such as 5G, cloud, and automotive, and Inphi's former CEO, Dr. Ford Tamer, has joined Marvell's board.

Title: Marvell's $10bn acquisition of Inphi closes
Summary: Marvell Technology has completed its $10 billion acquisition of Inphi Corporation, diversifying its chip offerings to include fiber-optic data traffic in addition to copper-based cables. The deal strengthens Marvell's leadership in 5G, Cloud, and Automotive markets, with Inphi's CEO joining Marvell's Board of Directors. The combined entity is valued at approximately $40 billion and funded with $4 billion in debt.

Title: Marvell Technology's Strong Growth Prospects Make its Stock a Buy
Summary: Marvell Technology recently completed its acquisition of Inphi, a move expected to significantly boost its position in the data center and 5G markets. Analysts have a positive outlook on MRVL stock, with a majority recommending "buy" and expecting substantial revenue and EPS growth in the coming fiscal years. The acquisition is projected to create a $40 billion semiconductor powerhouse and make Marvell stock an attractive investment, especially compared to its peers in terms of EV-to-sales multiple.

Title: Appleby team acted as legal counsel to Marvell Technology
Summary: A team from Appleby served as Cayman Islands and Bermuda legal counsel to global semiconductor company Marvell Technology Inc. for a corporate restructuring related to its $10 billion acquisition of Inphi Corporation. The acquisition, completed last month, created a "US semiconductor powerhouse" domiciled in the United States. The Appleby legal team was led by corporate partner Jacob MacAdam and included Jerome Wilson, Vance Power, and Riley O’ Brien.

Title: Marvell Introduces Bravera SSD Controllers to Enable the Highest Performing Data Center Flash Storage Solutions
Summary: Marvell has unveiled its new Bravera SC5 SSD controller family, which are the industry's first PCIe 5.0 SSD controllers. These controllers are designed to offer unprecedented performance, efficiency, and security for cloud data center workloads, boasting double the performance of PCIe 4.0 SSDs. They also include features like FIPS-compliant root of trust, AES 256-bit encryption, and a hardware-based Elastic SLA Enforcer to ensure quality of service and optimized resource utilization for hyperscale cloud providers.

Title: Marvell Extends PAM4 DSP Cloud Data Center Leadership with Industry's First Integrated Solution
Summary: Marvell has announced its Atlas 50Gbps PAM4 DSP chipset solution, which integrates transimpedance amplifiers and laser drivers into a single mainstream CMOS technology solution. This advancement significantly reduces power consumption by 25% and simplifies the supply chain for high-performance cloud data centers, computing, and AI applications. The Atlas DSP platform is designed for high-volume markets, offering cost-effective, highly integrated, and reliable technology essential for massive data center growth.

Title: Marvell Launches Industry's First 1.6T Ethernet PHY with 100G PAM4 I/Os in 5nm for Cloud Data Centers
Summary: Marvell has introduced the industry's first 1.6T Ethernet PHY with 100G PAM4 electrical I/Os, fabricated using a 5nm process, targeting cloud data centers. This new Alaska C PHY doubles the bandwidth of previous generations, enabling greater power efficiency and scalability for demanding applications like AI and machine learning. The solution supports 100G serial interconnects and is compliant with IEEE 802.3ck standards and the Ethernet Technology Consortium's 800GbE specifications.

Title: Marvell Announces 400G DSP to Proliferate Adoption of Coherent Pluggable Modules from Cloud to Access
Summary: Marvell has expanded its Coherent Digital Signal Processor (CDSP) portfolio with the new Deneb ultra-low power, multi-mode 400G DSP. This technology aims to advance disaggregated optical architectures and accelerate the adoption of IP-over-DWDM (IPoDWDM) for data center interconnects. Deneb facilitates an open ecosystem and supports a broad range of interoperable, standards-based coherent pluggable transceivers for cloud, access, and DCI transport networks.

Title: Wendy's Joins Meme Stocks, Marvell Rises as Tech Stocks Gain
Summary: Wendy's (WEN) has become the latest "meme stock," seeing its shares surge due to interest from retail investors on social media platforms. Marvell Technology (MRVL) is also experiencing gains, contributing to a broader rise in tech stocks. The overall market is facing a mixed open following disappointing global economic data.

Title: MWC 2021: Marvell OCTEON 10 DPU Launch Injects Innovation Boost to DPU Technology
Summary: Marvell has launched its OCTEON 10 DPU, designed to accelerate various security, networking, and storage workloads for 5G, cloud, carrier, and enterprise data centers. This new DPU aims to offer significant TCO advantages with innovations like the 5nm process, Arm Neoverse N2 cores, inline AI/ML hardware acceleration, and an integrated 1 terabit switch, targeting three times the performance and 50 percent lower power than previous generations. The OCTEON 10 is positioned as a frontrunner in DPU technology, addressing the increasing demand for data-centric compute and critical for meeting evolving market needs.

Title: Auto software company Sonatus raises $35 million from Hyundai Motor Group, SAIC Capital
Summary: Sonatus, a California-grown automotive software company founded in 2018, has successfully raised $35 million in a Series A funding round. This round was led by Silicon Valley VC Translink Capital and saw significant investment from industry giants including Hyundai Motor Group’s Kia Corporation, SAIC Capital, and LG Electronics. The company plans to use these funds to expand its market presence, forge new partnerships with OEMs, and grow its teams, as it aims to establish its vehicle software as a "data center on wheels."

Title: Marvell to Acquire Innovium - Accelerates Cloud Growth with Expanded Ethernet Switching Portfolio
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. announced its definitive agreement to acquire Innovium, Inc. in an all-stock transaction valued at $1.1 billion. This acquisition is set to significantly expand Marvell's Ethernet switching portfolio in the cloud data center market, adding approximately $150 million in incremental revenue for the next fiscal year and positioning Marvell as a key supplier for Tier 1 cloud customers. The transaction is expected to be neutral to Marvell's non-GAAP earnings per share in the first full quarter post-closing and accretive in the first full fiscal year thereafter.

Title: Marvell to Acquire Innovium - EE Times India
Summary: Marvell Technology Inc. is acquiring Innovium Inc., a provider of networking solutions for cloud and edge data centers, in an all-stock transaction. This acquisition will allow Marvell to expand into the fastest-growing segment of the switch market with a cloud-optimized solution, and Innovium is expected to become a significant supplier for a Tier 1 cloud customer in 2022. The deal is projected to add approximately $150 million in incremental revenue for Marvell next fiscal year.

Title: Marvell Tech to acquire Innovium for $1.1 Billion
Summary: Marvell Technology is set to acquire networking chip startup Innovium for $1.1 billion to enhance its market share in networking chips for large cloud-computing companies and data centers. The acquisition aims to bolster Marvell's portfolio, particularly with Innovium's Teralynx chips, which compete with Broadcom in the market for data center traffic controllers. This move follows Marvell's previous $10 billion acquisition of Inphi Corp, indicating a strategic effort to expand its cloud business offerings amid significant consolidation in the semiconductor industry.

Title: Here's why Marvell is acquiring chip startup Innovium in $1.1B deal
Summary: Marvell Technology is acquiring chip startup Innovium in a $1.1 billion deal to bolster its cloud business. This acquisition aligns with Marvell's strategic focus on the cloud sector. The deal follows other significant moves by Marvell, including its $10 billion Inphi acquisition.

Title: Marvell Technology stock slides as outlook overshadows earnings beat
Summary: Marvell Technology Group Ltd. shares experienced a slide in after-hours trading despite an earnings beat, as part of the chip maker's outlook fell below Wall Street's consensus. This decline occurred amidst a global chip shortage. Marvell's stock, trading under the symbol MRVL, fell 4% after hours following a minor gain during the regular session.

Title: Customizable RISC-V chip startup Ventana exits stealth with $38M in funding
Summary: Ventana Micro Systems Inc., a startup focused on customizable RISC-V chips, has emerged from stealth mode with $38 million in Series B funding, bringing its total raised to $53 million. The company designs CPUs based on the open-source RISC-V instruction set to optimize performance for cloud workloads, emphasizing flexibility, customizability, and significant cost savings compared to proprietary alternatives. Ventana aims to capitalize on the industry trend moving towards infrastructure and domain-specific processors, promising a "huge leap forward" in chip performance and development time with its chiplet-based strategy.

Title: Marvell Completes Acquisition of Innovium
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. announced the completion of its acquisition of Innovium, Inc., a leading provider of networking solutions for cloud and edge data centers. This acquisition strengthens Marvell's position in the cloud market and enables immediate participation in the fastest-growing segment of the switch market with a cloud-optimized solution. The transaction broadens Marvell's portfolio of silicon solutions targeting cloud data centers.

Title: Marvell Extends Data Infrastructure Leadership with TSMC 3nm Platform
Summary: Marvell announced its leadership in data infrastructure silicon by introducing a new advanced silicon platform utilizing TSMC's 3nm process technology. This platform offers superior power, performance, and area, enabling customers to develop unique, system-optimized solutions for various markets, including cloud data centers and 5G carriers. Marvell's comprehensive standards-based silicon platform integrates advanced die-to-die interface IP and TSMC's CoWoS packaging technology, providing cutting-edge multi-chip solutions.

Title: Marvell Completes Acquisition of Innovium
Summary: Marvell Technology Inc. has completed its acquisition of Innovium Inc., a leading provider of networking solutions for cloud and edge data centers. This acquisition significantly broadens Marvell's portfolio of silicon solutions, enhancing its leadership in cloud infrastructure and allowing it to immediately compete in the rapidly growing switch market with a cloud-optimized offering. Marvell aims to leverage this acquisition to further its mission of enabling next-generation enterprise, cloud, automotive, and carrier architectures.

Title: Lark Health flying high with $100M boost to invest in R&D, tech integrations with payers
Summary: Lark Health has secured $100 million in Series D funding, led by Deerfield Management Company, to expand its research and development and integrate its virtual care solutions more deeply with health plans. The company, which uses AI, coaching, and health tracking to manage chronic conditions, plans to enhance its data science and conversational AI platform for additional disease states. This investment will also help Lark expand its reach, which currently includes nearly 2 million individuals, into new markets and better serve underserved populations through its scalable, cost-effective personalized care.

Title: Marvell Unveils Brightlane Automotive Ethernet Innovations to Accelerate the Software-Defined Vehicle Era
Summary: Marvell has introduced its new 88QB5224 multi-gig Ethernet camera bridge solution, designed to enable best-in-class video distribution in software-defined vehicles. This innovation, part of Marvell's Brightlane automotive portfolio, supports various Ethernet standards and aims to provide a standardized, scalable, and secure backbone for in-vehicle networks, moving away from proprietary protocols for high-speed camera communication. The solution allows for the aggregation of up to four cameras through a single device, addressing the increasing demand for high-bandwidth interfaces as automotive camera resolutions grow.

Title: Marvell Technology Earnings Were Better Than Expected. The Stock Jumps 20%.
Summary: Marvell Technology's stock rose significantly after the infrastructure chip maker reported better-than-expected earnings and provided a strong outlook. The positive financial results and future projections led to a 20% jump in its stock during early trading.

Title: San Jose data connectivity business Credo Technology Group files plans to go public
Summary: Credo Technology Group, a San Jose-based data connectivity business, has filed plans to go public. The company, led by CEO Bill Brennan, specializes in providing chips and cables for high-speed data transmission and was founded by former Marvell Technology executives. This move signals a significant step for the company in the new year.

Title: Marvell Expands Interconnect Portfolio with Industry's 1st Cloud-Optimized 400G/800G PAM4 DSPs for Active Electrical Cables
Summary: Marvell has introduced its Alaska A PAM4 DSP family, the industry's first cloud-optimized 400G/800G DSPs for Active Electrical Cables (AECs), to address increasing bandwidth demands in cloud data centers driven by AI and ML. Fabricated in 6nm process, these DSPs leverage Marvell's PAM4 DSP technology to enable longer reach and thinner AECs, crucial for high-density data center deployments. This expansion aims to support the industry's transition to 100G/lane-based products and has garnered broad support from major cable manufacturers.

Title: Marvell Targets Cloud Data Centers with Silicon Photonics Platform
Summary: Marvell Technology has introduced its production-ready 400G DR4 silicon photonics platform, targeting cloud data centers to meet increasing bandwidth demands and support AI/ML applications. This platform aims to reduce costs, improve power efficiency, and accelerate market entry by leveraging silicon manufacturing processes. Marvell's approach integrates modulators and detectors monolithically in silicon, enabling advanced 2.5D/3D integration for enhanced performance and smaller form factors in optical interconnects spanning various distances.

Title: d-Matrix gets $44m in quest for efficient AI server chiplets
Summary: d-Matrix, a US chip startup, has raised $44 million from investors including Microsoft, SK Hynix, and Marvell Technology to develop efficient AI server chiplets. The company plans to use a "digital in-memory computing" architecture for its processors, aiming to outperform CPUs and GPUs for large transformer models in hyperscale and edge datacenters. Their initial roadmap includes chiplets code-named Nighthawk and Jayhawk, leveraging a Hetero-Modular organic packaging technology.

Title: d-Matrix Closes $44 Million in Series A
Summary: d-Matrix, a Santa Clara-based leader in high-efficiency AI compute for data centers, has secured $44 million in Series A funding. The round was led by Playground Global, with participation from M12 (Microsoft Venture Fund) and SK Hynix, as well as existing investors Nautilus Venture Partners, Marvell Technology, and Entrada Ventures. This investment will support product roadmap expansion and team growth across the United States, Australia, and India, and coincides with the announcement of their new silicon chiplet NighthawkTM, based on DIMC technology.

Title: Marvell Bolsters Cloud-Optimized CXL Portfolio with Acquisition of Tanzanite
Summary: Marvell has announced the acquisition of Tanzanite Silicon Solutions, Inc., a developer of advanced Compute Express Link (CXL) technologies. This all-cash transaction aims to strengthen Marvell's CXL development initiatives and integrate them into its cloud-optimized silicon solutions portfolio. The acquisition will leverage CXL to enable fully composable cloud infrastructure, improving resource utilization and reducing total cost of ownership for data centers, especially for demanding workloads like AI and machine learning.

Title: Marvell (MRVL) Enhances CXL Portfolio With Tanzanite Buyout
Summary: Marvell Technology announced its acquisition of Tanzanite Silicon Solutions Inc. in an all-cash transaction to strengthen its Compute Express Link (CXL) technology portfolio. This move is expected to enhance Marvell's cloud data center business by integrating CXL across its silicon offerings, improving data center efficiency, scalability, and flexibility. The acquisition aligns with Marvell's strategy of increasing investments in the data center business through strategic buyouts like Cavium, Inphi Corporation, and Innovium.

Title: Why Marvell bought interconnect upstart Tanzanite
Summary: Marvell Technology has acquired Tanzanite, a CXL startup specializing in memory expansion and pooling, to accelerate its composable infrastructure ambitions. The acquisition aims to disaggregate compute, memory, and storage resources, allowing them to be composed on the fly for memory-intensive workloads like AI/ML. While achieving fully composable data centers will take time, Marvell believes CXL technology will be crucial for integrating accelerators across its product portfolio and overcoming latency challenges associated with extending CXL benefits beyond server chassis.

Title: Marvell Injects New CXL Technology into Cloud-Optimized CXL Portfolio with Tanzanite Acquisition
Summary: Marvell has acquired Tanzanite Silicon Solutions, a developer of Compute Express Link (CXL) technologies, in an all-cash transaction. This acquisition strengthens Marvell's cloud-optimized silicon portfolio, expanding its addressable market and bolstering its ability to deliver fully composable cloud infrastructure. The move is seen as strategic to control Tanzanite's CXL technology, advance disaggregated architectures, and preclude rivals from acquiring these assets.

Title: Broadcom Vs. Marvell: Better Chipmaker Company To Buy (NASDAQ:AVGO)
Summary: This article compares Broadcom (AVGO) and Marvell (MRVL) primarily focusing on their semiconductor businesses. It concludes that Marvell has an edge in ASICs and processor technology, while Broadcom excels in analog business and demonstrates a superior M&A strategy with better revenue contribution and margins. The analysis aims to determine the better chipmaker company to buy.

Title: Marvell Introduces Industry's First Automotive Ethernet Switch with Lockstep Dual-Core Reliability for Safer Vehicles
Summary: Marvell has unveiled its third-generation Brightlane Ethernet Switch, an advanced automotive secure managed switch featuring lockstep dual-core Arm processing for enhanced reliability in mission-critical vehicle safety applications. This new switch integrates comprehensive security features, increased bandwidth, and port counts, supporting the transition to software-defined vehicles. It is designed to meet ISO 26262 ASIL-B safety standards and incorporates MACsec protocols and an embedded Hardware Security Module for robust data protection.

Title: Semiconductor giant Marvell plans ‘significant expansion’ of Kanata footprint after acquisition
Summary: Marvell, a U.S. semiconductor company, is significantly expanding its presence in Canada, particularly in Kanata, following its acquisition of local microchip design firms. The company plans to build out its offices in Ottawa, Toronto, and Vancouver to develop semiconductor technology for cloud, 5G, and automotive markets. Marvell expects to leverage Ottawa's tech talent and academic partnerships for its growth, with a focus on cutting-edge technologies.

Title: Who's growing faster than Nvidia and AMD? Rising datacenter star Marvell
Summary: Marvell Technology significantly outpaced other major fabless chip designers like AMD, Nvidia, and Qualcomm in the first quarter, achieving 72% semiconductor revenue growth. This rapid growth was largely driven by its acquisition of Innovium, a switch ASIC business catering to hyperscale data centers. Marvell is strategically shifting its focus from consumer markets to data infrastructure, with datacenter products now accounting for 44% of its total revenue, reinforcing its long-term growth strategy in cloud, 5G, and automotive sectors.

Title: Meet Chinese billionaire Weili Dai, one of the US’s richest self-made women
Summary: Weili Dai, a Shanghai-born "tech geek," moved to the US at 17 with no English and fulfilled her American dream by becoming a billionaire through her work in semiconductors. She co-founded Marvell Technology and has invested in several other companies. With a US$1.4 billion fortune, Dai was named one of America's richest self-made women by Forbes in 2022.

Title: Meet Chinese billionaire Weili Dai, one of the US’s richest self-made women
Summary: Weili Dai, a Shanghai-born "technology geek," became a billionaire through her work in semiconductors, co-founding Marvell Technology and later investing in and co-founding other tech companies. She is featured on Forbes' 2022 list of 25 richest American self-made women, alongside celebrities like Kim Kardashian and Rihanna. Dai's journey includes moving to the US at 17, learning English, and attending UC Berkeley, where she met her husband and business partner, Sehat Sutardja.

Title: Popstar Rihanna Becomes America’s Youngest Self-made Billionaire Woman; Taylor Swift Joins The Richest List
Summary: Rihanna has become America's youngest self-made billionaire woman at 34, with a net worth of $1.4 billion, primarily from her music and Fenty Beauty ventures. She is ranked 21st on Forbes' list of self-made billionaire women 2022. The article also highlights other celebrities like Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, and Celine Dion who made it onto the list, emphasizing the growing presence of successful women entrepreneurs.

Title: Sorry, Kylie Jenner: Rihanna Has Been Named the Youngest Female Self-Made Billionaire
Summary: Rihanna has been named the youngest female self-made billionaire by Forbes, with an estimated net worth of $1.4 billion. This title was previously held by Kylie Jenner, but Forbes later recalculated Jenner's net worth down to just under $900 million. Rihanna's fortune primarily comes from her music career and her successful businesses, Fenty Beauty and Savage X Fenty.

Title: MRVL Forecast — Price Target — Prediction for 2027
Summary: This article provides a forecast for Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) stock, including its price target for 2027 based on analyst ratings. It discusses recent EPS performance, revenue forecasts, and an overall "buy" rating from 46 analysts. The article emphasizes that this information should not be taken as investment advice.

Title: Marvell Unveils LiquidSecurity 2 HSM: Up to 1,000,000 AES Ops/s
Summary: Marvell has introduced its next-generation LiquidSecurity 2 Hardware Security Module (HSM), designed to significantly accelerate cryptography workloads for cloud datacenters. This PCIe 4.0 x8 card utilizes Marvell's Octeon DPU hardware and can perform up to 1,000,000 GCM ops/s, 42,000 RSA-2K ops/s, and 100,000 ECC P-256 ops/s while consuming only 35W-50W. The new HSM offers enhanced performance, multi-tenancy support, and future-proof upgradeability for various security certifications.

Title: Marvell Launches LiquidSecurity 2 Module to Empower Best-in-Class HSM-as-a-Service for the Multi-Cloud Era
Summary: Marvell has announced its LiquidSecurity 2 (LS2) hardware security module (HSM) adapter, designed to provide advanced encryption, key management, and authentication services in the cloud. This new solution offers significantly improved performance and key storage capacity, aiming to lower the total cost of ownership for cloud service providers and large enterprises by enabling HSM-as-a-service. It supports modern security requirements, including cryptographic agility and future-proofing against new vulnerabilities, making cloud-based encryption more accessible and efficient.

Title: Marvell Readies Hardware Security-as-a-Service for Prime Time with LiquidSecurity 2 Launch
Summary: Marvell has launched its LiquidSecurity 2 (LS2) hardware security module (HSM) adapter, designed to facilitate the transition from on-premise HSMs to multi-cloud and private cloud environments. The LS2 offers significant performance improvements, including 12 times faster ECC operations, support for up to one million encryption keys, and 45 partitions for multi-tenant use cases. This solution aims to help organizations meet growing security and compliance requirements by providing robust cryptographic acceleration and secure key management in a cloud-optimized framework.

Title: Marvell Stock Can Thrive in a Downturn for Chips, Analyst Says
Summary: Barclays has indicated that Marvell Technology (MRVL) is positioned to perform well even amidst a significant downturn in the semiconductor industry. This positive outlook follows a similar optimistic assessment from J.P. Morgan last week, suggesting that Marvell is seen as a "relative winner" in a challenging chip market.

Title: Vodafone and Samsung cooperate with Marvell to accelerate Open RAN performance and adoption
Summary: Vodafone, Samsung Electronics, and Marvell are collaborating to enhance 5G Open Radio Access Networks (RAN) performance and adoption in Europe. This partnership integrates Marvell’s OCTEON Fusion® processor into standard Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) servers, paired with Samsung's virtualized RAN software, to improve data processing, energy efficiency, and overall network performance. The goal is to make Open RAN systems comparable to, or even outperform, traditional single-supplier radio networks, while also strengthening the vendor supply chain and promoting ecosystem innovation.

Title: American chip firm Marvell cuts jobs in China amid deepening tech rivalry
Summary: US chip designer Marvell Technology Group is scaling down its operations in China, resulting in job eliminations, following a similar move by Micron Technology. This decision reflects the increasing geopolitical tensions and Beijing's strict COVID-19 controls, which are diminishing China's appeal as an R&D base for global tech companies. Multiple departments in Marvell's Shanghai and Chengdu offices are expected to be cut or downsized.

Title: Observers: China’s Chip Talent Hurdle Worsens After Layoffs at US Firm Marvell
Source: VOA - Voice of America English News
Summary: US chipmaker Marvell Technology is eliminating R&D staff in China, following similar moves by other American firms, exacerbating China's talent shortage in cutting-edge chip design and manufacturing. This comes amidst intensifying US-China tech rivalry and new Biden administration curbs on chip exports and US persons working in Chinese chip firms. Experts believe this trend will force China to adapt to a new globalized tech landscape and accelerate its efforts to develop indigenous chip capabilities.

Title: Industry Ministry, U.S. Firm to Cooperate on Semiconductor Industry Development
Summary: Indonesia's Industry Ministry is partnering with a United States company, Zerro Power, co-founded by innovator Sehat Sutardja, to establish an integrated circuit design center. This collaboration aims to reduce Indonesia's dependence on semiconductor imports and develop an independent national semiconductor industry. The initiative is part of broader efforts to secure the semiconductor supply chain amidst increasing global demand.

Title: Marvell Stock Sinks as Earnings Fall Short. Customers Are Pulling Back.
Summary: Marvell Technology's shares fell sharply after the company reported disappointing earnings and outlook. The data-center semiconductor firm cited reduced stockpiles of chips by storage equipment makers as a reason for its near-term struggles. This news led to a significant drop in Marvell's stock value, which had already lost nearly half its value this year.

Title: Marvell, Nokia upgrade ReefShark SoC chipset for 5G
Summary: Marvell and Nokia have deepened their partnership to upgrade Nokia's ReefShark system-on-chip portfolio, aiming to deliver an advanced radio access and transport processing platform. This collaboration leverages Marvell's 5nm Arm Neoverse N2 multi-core solution and Octeon 10 DPU, enabling high performance and low latency for new 5G services while working to minimize costs and energy consumption. The upgraded chipsets are crucial for meeting the increasing demands of wireless connectivity in 5G networks.

Title: Weili Dai’s Secret Weapon for Success: Be Fair and Care!
Summary: Weili Dai, co-founder of Marvell Technology and founder of MeetKai, attributes her success in the semiconductor industry to a philosophy of "Be fair and care," learned from her parents. She applies this principle to her business practices and investments, prioritizing ethical engagement and focusing on mutual success with partners and customers. Dai also champions women's contributions to technology, particularly in AI development, emphasizing the creation of humane and accessible solutions to improve lives.

Title: Marvell Announces CFO Transition | Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL)
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) announced the appointment of Willem Meintjes as Chief Financial Officer, effective January 20, 2023. Meintjes, formerly Chief Accounting Officer and Treasurer, succeeds Jean Hu, who is departing for another opportunity. The company also reaffirmed the midpoint of its Q4 fiscal 2023 revenue outlook, narrowing the range to +/- 3%.

Title: AMD, Marvell Technology Name New CFOs
Summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Marvell Technology have announced new Chief Financial Officers. Jean Hu, previously CFO at Marvell Technology, is moving to AMD for the same role. Willem Meintjes will take over as CFO at Marvell Technology, effective January 20th.

Title: Nvidia, Broadcom, and Marvell Are Chip Stocks to Benefit in AI Arms Race
Summary: J.P. Morgan analysts have identified Nvidia, Broadcom, and Marvell as three semiconductor companies poised to benefit significantly from the increasing demand for artificial intelligence services and software. This projection comes amidst what is described as an "AI arms race." The Street Notes section highlights how this trend is expected to lift these chip stocks.

Title: Marvell and AWS Collaborate to Enable Cloud-First Silicon Design
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. has selected Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its cloud provider for electronic design automation (EDA). This collaboration enables Marvell to rapidly scale its EDA processes in the cloud, addressing the increasing complexity of chip design and accelerating time to market. Marvell continues to be a strategic semiconductor supplier for AWS, providing cloud-optimized silicon for data center infrastructure.

Title: Marvell Announces Cloud-Optimized 51.2 Tbps Networking Platform for AI/ML and Data Center Networks
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) has announced a new cloud-optimized 51.2 Tbps networking platform designed to address bottlenecks in AI/ML and cloud data center networks. This platform, consisting of the Teralynx® 10 switch chip and the Nova™ 1.6 Tbps electro-optics platform, offers four times the bandwidth of current solutions. It aims to reduce time-in-networking, maximize compute utilization, and meet the escalating bandwidth demands of AI and ML applications by improving density, reducing power, and lowering cost per bit.

Title: Marvell to Showcase Cloud-Optimized Electro-Optics and Networking at OFC 2023
Summary: Marvell Technology will participate in the 2023 Optical Networking and Communication (OFC) Conference from March 5-9, 2023, showcasing its cloud-optimized electro-optics and networking solutions. The company will feature demonstrations of its Nova 1.6T PAM4 electro-optics platform, Teralynx and Prestera switch silicon, and various pluggable optical modules, along with participating in interoperability demonstrations and various presentations and panels.

Title: Avigdor Willenz breaks his silence
Summary: Israeli billionaire Avigdor Willenz, responsible for major chip company exits, has broken his silence from Switzerland, where he moved two years ago. He criticizes Israel's political discourse and government actions, expressing deep concern for the country's future and lamenting the erosion of its moral and liberal values. Willenz, while remaining an Israeli citizen, has stopped new investments in Israel and advocates for a new civil agreement, possibly through a canton system, to address societal divisions.

Title: Marvell Stock Price Prediction: Will MRVL Fall Below the $50 Mark?
Summary: Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) stock has experienced a recent decline, with its price decreasing by 4.14% over the past week, despite a strong year-to-date return of 65.37%. Financial analysis shows challenges in profitability, with a negative average annual earnings growth, though revenues have increased. Technical indicators like RSI, MACD, and EMA suggest a bearish outlook for the short-term, with potential support levels identified at $61.21 and $56.54.

Title: US semiconductor firm Marvell to open new facility in Vietnam
Summary: U.S. semiconductor firm Marvell Technology announced plans to open a new facility in Vietnam by the end of 2024, aiming to establish a world-class design center in Ho Chi Minh City. This expansion includes a commitment to increase its Vietnamese workforce by 50% in three years and double funding for its scholarship program to address the country's severe shortage of skilled semiconductor engineers. The announcement was made during the U.S.-Vietnam Innovation and Investment Summit, highlighting Vietnam's growing role as a semiconductor innovation hub.

Title: Tech Jam: The future is here
Summary: The Vermont Tech Jam, an annual career and tech expo, is scheduled for October 21st, showcasing various tech companies and job opportunities in Vermont. The event will feature a job fair, robotics demonstrations, flight simulators, and discussions on cellular agriculture, including lab-grown meat. The Tech Jam is supported by numerous companies and organizations committed to the local tech ecosystem.

Title: Construction platform Gravel raises US$14 million funding round
Summary: Indonesian construction startup Gravel has successfully raised US$14 million in a funding round, attracting investments from venture capital firms New Enterprise Associates, SMDV, and East Ventures, along with notable individual investors. The company's platform connects 1.7 million skilled construction workers with contractors and architects, having supported over 6,000 projects across Indonesia. Gravel plans to use the new funds for business expansion, market reach, and developing a predictive model for construction progress monitoring.

Title: Two New Marvell OCTEON 10 Processors Bring Server-Class Performance to Networking Devices
Summary: Marvell Technology has introduced two new OCTEON 10 data processing units (DPUs), the OCTEON 10 CN102 and CN103, designed to bring server-class performance and efficiency to networking devices. These 5 nm DPUs, featuring up to eight Arm Neoverse N2 cores, offer significant performance improvements and power reduction for applications in routers, firewalls, and 5G infrastructure. Several major networking equipment manufacturers are already integrating these new processors into their product designs.

Title: Intel, Marvell, Agilent Technologies advise state of layoffs
Summary: Three Silicon Valley technology companies — Intel, Marvell, and Agilent Technologies — have notified California officials of upcoming job cuts. A total of 166 positions are set to be eliminated across these companies.

Title: Marvell Tech sees India as R&D center for advanced CMOS and other chips
Summary: Marvell Technology is focusing its R&D efforts on advanced CMOS technologies, including 5nm, 3nm, and 2nm processes, with India serving as its largest R&D center outside the US. The company is heavily invested in data infrastructure products, particularly for AI-centric data centers, emphasizing improved computing power, storage, and connectivity while optimizing energy efficiency. Marvell's strategic acquisitions and significant expansion in India across Pune, Bangalore, and Hyderabad underline the country's crucial role in its product development and overall growth trajectory.

Title: Marvell Technology: Not Overly Bullish Ahead Of The Q4 Event
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. has seen impressive stock returns over the past year, largely driven by its data center segment. While the company's Q4 2024 results are anticipated on March 7th, the enterprise and carrier segments are expected to be weak. The article suggests that despite potential cost improvements, the increasing share of custom silicon in revenue may temper gross profit progression next year, making the current valuation and technical indicators not ideal for a long position.

Title: Marvell CEO Matthew Murphy sells shares worth over $1.9 million
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. CEO Matthew J. Murphy sold 30,000 shares of company stock for over $1.9 million on March 14, 2024, through a pre-arranged 10b5-1 trading plan. Despite the sale, Murphy retains a significant stake, and analysts project profitability for the company this year, although some have revised earnings forecasts downwards. Marvell Technology currently has a market capitalization of $58.54 billion and has shown strong price total returns over the last year.

Title: Marvell Extends 1.6T Connectivity Leadership With Industry's First PAM4 Optical DSP Integrating 200 Gbps Electrical and Optical Interfaces
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) has introduced Nova 2, the industry's first 1.6 Tbps PAM4 optical DSP with 200 Gbps electrical and optical interfaces, designed to meet the growing performance demands of AI and cloud infrastructure. This new DSP, along with the previously announced flagship Nova optical DSP, enables a doubling of optical module bandwidth compared to current 800 Gbps modules, optimizing connectivity for next-generation data centers and AI clusters. Nova 2 is currently sampling to select customers, with the original Nova DSP generally available.

Title: Marvell Demonstrates Industry's First 200G 3D Silicon Photonics Engine to Scale Accelerated Infrastructure
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. has demonstrated its 3D Silicon Photonics (SiPho) Engine, which is the industry's first highly integrated SiPho engine featuring 32 channels of 200G electrical and optical interfaces. This technology is designed to enable higher density, lower power optical interconnects for next-generation AI clusters and cloud data centers, delivering twice the bandwidth and 30% lower power per bit compared to current 100 Gbps devices. The SiPho engine integrates hundreds of components into a single device, addressing the increasing bandwidth demands of AI services.

Title: Better Chip Stock: Marvell Technology vs. Qualcomm
Summary: This article compares Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Qualcomm (QCOM) as semiconductor stock investments. Marvell, despite a near-term slowdown, is driven by AI-oriented chips and acquisitions, while Qualcomm is recovering from a smartphone market downturn with diversification into automotive and IoT, alongside new AI mobile chips. The author concludes that Qualcomm is the better buy due to its lower valuation, higher dividend yield, and anticipated market recovery.

Title: Marvell Technology (MRVL) Outperforms Broader Market: What You Need to Know
Summary: Marvell Technology (MRVL) saw its stock rise by 1.55% in the most recent trading session, outperforming the S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq. Despite recent losses over the past month, the semiconductor company is projected to report a decline in EPS and revenue for its upcoming earnings release. Analysts' estimates for Marvell Technology have shown a slight upward revision, though the company currently holds a Zacks Rank of #4 (Sell), with its valuation metrics (Forward P/E and PEG ratio) indicating a premium compared to its industry.

Title: Alchip says revenue to grow in 2026
Summary: AI chip designer Alchip Technologies Ltd expects significant revenue growth in 2026, driven by a new major AI chip customer, despite a stock price drop and increasing competition. The company emphasizes its strong partnerships with cloud service providers and its unique capabilities in leading-edge process technologies (5nm, 4nm, 3nm) for ASIC design. Alchip also reported a 104% increase in net profit for the last quarter and is prioritizing advanced packaging capacity from TSMC to meet AI chip production demands.

Title: Marvell Expands Connectivity Portfolio With New PCIe Retimer Product Line to Scale Compute Fabrics of Accelerated Infrastructure
Summary: Marvell Technology Inc. has launched its new Alaska P PCIe retimer product line, designed to scale data center compute fabrics in accelerated servers, CXL systems, and disaggregated infrastructure. These 8- and 16-lane PCIe Gen 6 retimers, built on Marvell's 5nm PAM4 technology, are crucial for connecting AI accelerators, GPUs, and CPUs as AI applications demand significantly higher bandwidth and faster data rates, necessitating reliable communication over greater distances. The new product line extends Marvell's PAM4 leadership beyond Ethernet and InfiniBand, addressing the growing market for PCIe and CXL connectivity within server systems with industry-leading low power consumption.

Title: Marvell Technology Data Center Revenues Surge, But the Rest Fall
Summary: Marvell Technology saw an 87% year-over-year jump in data center revenues, which now account for 70% of its total revenue, driven by the AI infrastructure boom. However, its other segments, including Carrier, Enterprise, Consumer, and Automotive/Industrial, experienced significant declines ranging from 13% to 75%. Despite beating revenue estimates, Marvell's stock dropped 10% due to these segment weaknesses and a conservative outlook, highlighting investor concern over its dependence on data center growth.

Title: Marvell Teralynx 10 51.2T Ethernet Switch Enters Volume Production for Global AI Cloud Deployments
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. announced that its Teralynx 10 Ethernet switch, a 51.2 Tbps device with ultra-low latency and low power consumption, has entered volume production with customer deployments already underway. This switch is designed for scaling accelerated infrastructure in AI cloud data centers, supporting the industry's shift towards open network operating systems like SONiC. Marvell expects shipments of 51.2 Tbps switches to increase significantly, emphasizing multi-vendor diversity and a unified platform for various network points.

Title: Marvell Introduces Breakthrough Structera CXL Product Line to Address Server Memory Bandwidth and Capacity Challenges in Cloud Data Centers
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. has launched its new Structera product line of Compute Express Link (CXL) devices to tackle memory performance and scaling issues in cloud data centers. The line includes Structera A CXL near-memory accelerators, optimized for high-bandwidth applications like deep learning with integrated Arm Neoverse processors, and Structera X CXL memory-expansion controllers, designed to add terabytes of memory for high-capacity applications and enable recycling of DDR4 DIMMs. These products are the first to support four memory channels, integrate inline compression, and are manufactured using a 5nm process, aiming to improve efficiency, reduce e-waste, and lower operational costs for cloud operators.

Title: Marvell presents Structera CXL product line targeting cloud data centres
Summary: Marvell Technology has launched the Structera CXL product line designed to help cloud data center operators address memory performance and scaling challenges. The line includes Structera A CXL near-memory accelerators for high-bandwidth applications like DLRM, and Structera X CXL memory-expansion controllers for high-capacity applications such as in-memory databases. These products aim to optimize resource utilization, lower energy consumption, and allow for the repurposing of older DDR4 DIMMs, thus reducing CapEx and promoting sustainability.

Title: RISC-V chip startup Akeana launches with $100M+ in funding
Summary: Akeana USA Inc., a RISC-V chip startup founded by former Marvell Technology engineers, launched with over $100 million in funding from investors like Kleiner Perkins, Mayfield, and Fidelity. The company offers a product line of CPU core designs based on the open-source RISC-V architecture, targeting various applications from IoT devices to data center servers. Akeana's designs are already being evaluated by several "tier one" customers.

Title: What You Need To Know Ahead of Marvell Technology's Earnings Report
Summary: Marvell Technology (MRVL) is scheduled to report its fiscal second-quarter earnings after the market closes on Thursday. Analysts anticipate a decline in revenue compared to the previous year but expect narrower losses. Investors will keenly watch for indications that the company's sales have bottomed out and for updates on its artificial intelligence initiatives, with Marvell's shares already up nearly 4% ahead of the announcement.

Title: Marvell Technology Stock Surges on Better-Than-Expected Sales, Boosted by AI Demand
Summary: Marvell Technology's stock surged nearly 5% after reporting better-than-expected fiscal Q2 2025 sales, primarily driven by strong demand for products supporting artificial intelligence. CEO Matt Murphy highlighted growth in electro-optics and ramping custom AI programs, leading to positive guidance for the third quarter. The company anticipates third-quarter diluted EPS of 40 cents (plus or minus 5 cents) and revenue of $1.45 billion (plus or minus $5 billion), exceeding analyst estimates.

Title: Marvell sees 5G sales slump but guides for second-half revival
Summary: Marvell Technology, a US chipmaker, has experienced a significant slump in its 5G sales due to telecommunications spending cuts and inventory build-up, particularly affecting its largest 5G customer, Nokia. Despite a challenging first half of the year with plummeting revenue in its carrier infrastructure unit, Marvell's CEO Matt Murphy projects a revival in the second half, especially in carrier infrastructure and enterprise networking, aiming for these divisions to collectively reach $2 billion to $2.2 billion annually. The company has also found some relief in its data-center business, which nearly doubled in size thanks to AI-related demand, helping to narrow overall losses.

Title: Sehat Sutardja, semiconductor pioneer and Marvell co-founder, has died
Summary: Sehat Sutardja, co-founder of Marvell Technology and a significant figure in the semiconductor industry, has passed away at 63. A UC Berkeley alumnus, Sutardja was a generous donor to Berkeley Engineering, contributing to the construction of Sutardja Dai Hall and supporting academic and research excellence. His legacy includes fostering a culture of innovation and making lasting impacts through his philanthropic efforts.

Title: Marvell co-founder Sehat Sutardja has died as industry mourns semiconductor visionary
Summary: Dr. Sehat Sutardja, co-founder of Marvell Technology, has passed away. Born in 1961, Sutardja was a semiconductor visionary, holding over 440 patents and co-founding Marvell in 1995 with his wife and brother. He later founded Silicon Box, an advanced semiconductor packaging company, in 2021.

Title: The life and chip works of Marvell co-founder Sehat Sutardja
Summary: This article chronicles the life and work of Marvell co-founder Sehat Sutardja, highlighting his contributions to the semiconductor industry, including his pioneering ideas on modular chips (chiplets). It covers his early fascination with electronics, his academic journey, the founding of Marvell Technology Group, and his later co-founding of Silicon Box, a chiplet foundry. The piece also touches on his personal qualities and enduring influence on the field.

Title: Marvel takes PCIe to Gen 7 on 3nm
Summary: Marvell Technology Inc. has demonstrated PCIe Gen 7 connectivity using 3nm silicon, enabling data transfer speeds of up to 128 gigatransfers per second (GT/s) per lane. This advancement, which utilizes PAM4 modulation, doubles the speed of PCIe Gen 6 and is designed to meet the performance demands of next-generation AI data centers and accelerated server platforms. Marvell is expanding its PAM4-based interconnect portfolio to include copper and optical PCIe, CXL, and proprietary compute fabric links.

Title: Marvell Statistics By Revenue, Total Assets, Future Readiness, Acquisitions And Products
Summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Marvell Technology's financial and operational performance, including its revenue, total assets, R&D expenses, future readiness, and key acquisitions. It highlights the company's consistent growth in revenue and assets, particularly noting a peak in revenue at $5.92 billion in 2023, driven by strategic investments in innovation and expansion into key markets like China and the US. The report also details Marvell's competitive standing in future readiness and a comprehensive list of its product offerings.

Title: Marvell Expands Strategic Collaboration with AWS to Enable Accelerated Infrastructure for AI in the Cloud
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. announced an expanded strategic collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS) through a five-year, multi-generational agreement. This partnership focuses on accelerating infrastructure for AI in the cloud by supplying Marvell's data center semiconductors and leveraging AWS's cloud infrastructure for Marvell's silicon design acceleration. The collaboration aims to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and speed up time-to-market for both companies.

Title: Why Marvell Technology is the next AI winner
Summary: Marvell Technology has seen its market value nearly double in the past year, largely due to its significant role in the booming AI infrastructure market. The company partners with all hyperscalers, particularly AWS, providing custom AI chips and infrastructure solutions. While not consistently profitable, its strategic positioning in AI has driven its stock market performance, with expectations to convert this into future profits.

Title: After Earnings, Is Marvell Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
Summary: Morningstar raised its fair value estimate for Marvell Technology to $90 per share after its Q3 earnings, driven by strong AI demand and better-than-expected forecasts. Despite optimistic growth projections, the stock is considered roughly 25% overvalued. The company holds a narrow economic moat due to intangible assets in networking chip design and is focused on deleveraging while investing in growth.

Title: Despite currently being unprofitable, Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) has delivered a 306% return to shareholders over 5 years
Summary: Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), despite being unprofitable, has provided a 306% return to shareholders over the past five years, reflecting strong revenue growth of 17% annually. The company's share price saw a significant 297% increase, and its Total Shareholder Return (TSR) climbed to 306% due to reinvested dividends. Recent insider buying and positive sentiment indicate a potentially strong future for the stock.

Title: Marvell Announces Breakthrough Co-Packaged Optics Architecture for Custom AI Accelerators
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) announced a new co-packaged optics (CPO) architecture for its custom XPU AI accelerators. This innovation enables higher bandwidth and longer reach scale-up fabric connections, enhancing AI server performance by allowing hundreds of XPUs across multiple racks, compared to tens within a single rack using traditional copper interconnects. The architecture integrates optical components directly into the XPU package, reducing signal loss, improving power efficiency, and supporting up to 100X longer connections with optimal latency.

Title: Is Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) the Best Growth Stock Under $100 to Buy Now?
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) is highlighted as a top growth stock under $100, ranked first on a list compiled by Insider Monkey. The company, a global semiconductor firm, reported record revenues in Q4 2025 and fiscal year 2025, largely driven by its data center segment and strong AI demand. Despite potential macroeconomic headwinds, Marvell's strong financial performance, including significant AI revenue growth and increasing custom silicon programs, positions it as a promising investment.

Title: Marvell Advances Interconnect Portfolio for Scale-up and Scale-out Fabrics at OFC 2025
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. announced it will showcase its advanced interconnect portfolio for AI deployments at OFC 2025, from March 31 to April 3 in San Francisco. The company will present technologies like 400G PAM4, co-packaged optics, 1.6T silicon photonics light engines, and 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggable optics. These innovations aim to deliver higher performance, customization, and flexibility for AI networks, addressing the anticipated market growth for interconnect chipsets expected to reach $11.5 billion by 2030.

Title: Marvell to Sell Automotive Ethernet Business to Infineon for $2.5 Billion in Cash
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. has announced a definitive agreement to sell its Automotive Ethernet business to Infineon Technologies AG for $2.5 billion in an all-cash transaction. This strategic move aims to deliver strong financial returns for Marvell shareholders, as the company increasingly focuses on data infrastructure solutions, with data centers driving a significant portion of its revenue. The transaction, which includes Marvell's Brightlane® Automotive Ethernet portfolio, is expected to close within calendar year 2025, pending regulatory approvals.

Title: Infineon Technologies to buy Marvell's auto ethernet business for $2.5 billion
Summary: German chipmaker Infineon Technologies announced its plans to acquire Marvell Technology's automotive ethernet business for approximately $2.5 billion in cash. This acquisition aims to expand Infineon's microcontroller segment and is expected to generate significant revenue and gross margin for its automotive division in 2025. The deal aligns with Marvell's strategy to focus on AI and custom silicon, while Infineon plans to finance the acquisition through additional debt.

Title: Is Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) a NASDAQ Stock with the Highest Upside Potential?
Summary: Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) is identified as a NASDAQ stock with significant upside potential, ranking first on a list compiled using analysts' upside potential and hedge fund sentiment. The article discusses Wedbush Securities' Dan Ives' concerns about tariffs and geopolitical tensions impacting tech supply chains and earnings, while highlighting Marvell's strong position in AI and cloud markets through partnerships like with Amazon Web Services. Bank of America reiterated a Buy rating on MRVL due to its AI opportunities and growth trajectory.

Title: Marvell Technology: Shares Plunge, But Operating Momentum Accelerates (NASDAQ:MRVL)
Summary: Marvell Technology's stock has significantly declined but the company's operating momentum is accelerating. While realistic earnings are modest due to stock-based compensation, the sale of its Automotive Ethernet business is expected to improve financial health. Despite improved valuations, caution is advised due to mixed business performance.

Title: Marvell Announces Changes to its Board of Directors
Summary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) announced changes to its Board of Directors, with Michael Strachan and Robert Switz deciding not to stand for reelection at the upcoming Annual Meeting of Stockholders on June 13, 2025. Summary: Marvell Technology, Microsoft, and Utimaco have partnered to launch Azure Payment HSM v2, an industry-first secure, cloud-scale payments solution. This platform combines Marvell LiquidSecurity HSMs, Utimaco Atalla Payments Module software, and Microsoft Azure to provide a fully managed payment security service. It aims to help financial institutions and payment service providers meet stringent PCI security, compliance, and operational requirements for regulated payment workloads without the overhead of managing physical HSM infrastructure.

Title: Marvell Jumps 5.2% as AI Optics Win More U.S. Capacity
Summary: Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) saw its shares jump 5.2% after securing a multiyear agreement with GlobalFoundries to expand silicon-germanium manufacturing capacity in Vermont. This partnership aims to strengthen Marvell's optical-networking supply for AI data centers, addressing the growing need to efficiently move vast amounts of data between powerful chips. While the deal's immediate financial impact is unclear, it positions Marvell to meet increasing demand for its AI-connectivity solutions despite the company's already high valuation.
